Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.01 U06 L06 GP Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.01 Slide note: Revision improves clarity. Which speaker note best supports the slide? \

answer.text: A. Revision improves clarity because the slide says it does.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This only repeats the slide without adding explanation.

answer.text: B. Revision is a word on this slide.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain the meaning of the slide.

answer.text: C. Revision helps writers make ideas easier to follow by improving word choice, transitions, and explanations.

feedback.text: Correct. This speaker note explains the slide instead of simply repeating it.

answer.text: D. I will read the slide now.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reading the slide aloud does not add meaningful oral explanation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.02 U06 L06 GP Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.02 Which slide note is best for an integrated oral and digital presentation? \

answer.text: A. A long paragraph with every planned sentence

feedback.text: Incorrect. Slides should not carry the whole speech.

answer.text: B. Feedback reveals unclear claims.

feedback.text: Correct. Review the lesson explanation to confirm why this choice fits or does not fit.

answer.text: C. Stuff about feedback and writing

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague to guide the audience.

answer.text: D. I will say something here.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not communicate a useful idea.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.V.03 U06 L06 GP Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.C.03 In a presentation, the word "credible" means which of the following? \

answer.text: A. confusing and unsupported

feedback.text: Incorrect. Credible information should be clear and supported.

answer.text: B. trustworthy and reliable

feedback.text: Correct. In this context, credible evidence is evidence the audience can trust.

answer.text: C. colorful and decorative

feedback.text: Incorrect. Color and decoration do not determine credibility.

answer.text: D. unrelated but interesting

feedback.text: Incorrect. Interesting information is not necessarily credible or relevant.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.L.01 U06 L06 GP Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.L.01 Which slide note uses standard English conventions? \

answer.text: A. Revision help writers make ideas clearer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The verb does not agree with the singular subject "Revision."

answer.text: B. Revision help writer's make ideas clear.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This has agreement and apostrophe errors.

answer.text: C. Revision helping writers make ideas clearer.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is a fragment rather than a complete sentence.

answer.text: D. Revision helps writers make ideas clearer.

feedback.text: Correct. The sentence uses correct subject-verb agreement.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: MLA.ENG1.C.03 U06 L06 GP Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.ENG1.V.03 Before sharing a collaborative digital presentation, what should students check? \

answer.text: A. Whether the presentation is polished, audience-aware, and ready to share

feedback.text: Correct. This matches publication-ready communication for a specific audience.

answer.text: B. Whether every slide has the most words possible

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication-ready work should be clear, not overcrowded.

answer.text: C. Whether the presentation uses random formatting

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random formatting weakens publication-ready quality.

answer.text: D. Whether speaker notes and slides are unrelated

feedback.text: Incorrect. Integrated communication requires connection between slides and oral explanation.
